Course Overview

This qualification reflects the role of community services workers iThis qualification reflects the role of workers in a range of community services who work autonomously, provide leadership and supervision, and support individuals, groups and communities.

Why Study This Qualification?

Through this qualification, you can develop skills in:

✔︎ Delivering support tailored to individual needs and goals
✔︎ Planning and coordinating community services
✔︎ Creating inclusive environments that respect diversity
✔︎ Encouraging community engagement and participation
✔︎ Supervising teams and supporting effective service delivery
✔︎ Assisting people experiencing complex challenges
✔︎ Promoting the rights and interests of individuals and communities
✔︎ Supporting people across aged care and community care environments

Career Outcomes

The Diploma of Community Services can help you develop skills relevant to a range of roles in the community services sector, depending on your experience and the requirements of each position.

  • Community Services Team Leader

  • Community Development Worker

  • Case Manager

  • Program Coordinator

  • Community Services Coordinator

  • Support Services Manager

  • Community Engagement Officer

  • Community Services Manager

Make a difference. Support individuals. Strengthen communities.

Entry Requirements

All applicants are required to complete a Pre-Training Review (PTR) (also referred to as the Upfront Assessment of Need), a Language, Literacy and Numeracy (LLND) assessment through CSPA, and an Enrolment Form.

This process assesses the applicant's suitability for the course, identifies any support needs, considers Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL) and Credit Transfer opportunities, and ensures the qualification is the most appropriate training pathway.

After completing this qualification, you may be able to pursue further studies in areas such as:

  • Bachelor of Social Work

  • Advanced Diploma of Community Sector Management

This qualification is delivered through a blended model combining real-time virtual classroom delivery and face-to-face component.

Learners undertaking any online or digitally supported components should have access to a suitable computer or device, reliable internet connection, email and commonly used document/PDF software. Specific technology requirements should be confirmed by Fran Capelli Academy for the final delivery model.

Students undertaking the CHC52025 Diploma of Community Services are required to complete 100 hours of work placement as part of their training.

Course Overview

This qualification is designed for students who want to become professional barbers without being employed under an apprenticeship contract. It provides the skills and knowledge required to perform a wide range of barbering services, including men’s haircutting, clipper techniques, beard and moustache design, shaving services, and men’s grooming. 

What will you learn?
  • Traditional and modern men's haircutting.
  • Clipper-over-comb and freehand clipper techniques.
  • Beard and moustache design and maintenance.
  • Head and face shaving.
  • Men's grooming services.
  • Client consultation and customer service.
  • Salon operations and workplace health and safety.
  • Basic hair coloring and highlighting services
Career Outcomes

After successful completion, graduates can seek employment as:
• Qualified Barber 
• Men's Grooming Specialist 
• Barbershop Professional 
• Salon Barber Specialist

SHB40216 Certificate IV in Hairdressing

Entry Requirements

All applicants are required to complete a Pre-Training Review (PTR), a Language, Literacy and Numeracy (LLND) assessment, and an Enrolment Form.

Key Features

  • Delivered through face-to-face practical training in a salon environment and virtual theory classes.
  • Students gain experience through practical observations, portfolios, and written assessments
On Completion of Course

Students completing all assessment requirements will be awarded SHB30516 Certificate III in Barbering

On Partial Completion of Course

Students who successfully complete part of the assessment requirements for the SHB30516 Certificate III in Barbering will receive a Statement of Attainment outlining the units of competency they have achieved.

Please note that awards will only be issued to students who have fulfilled all their financial obligations to Fran Capelli Academy.

For further information or to visit the Academy, please feel free to contact us on (03) 9818 0089.

Assessment Arrangements

Assessment Overview

This is a competency-based program, where assessment is conducted continuously throughout the course. Students are assessed until they either demonstrate competency in the required tasks or any identified learning gaps are addressed through further training.

Students are required to complete the written components of their assessments in their own time and submit them to their trainer by the specified due dates.

Assessment Requirements

Assessment requirements for each unit are clearly outlined on the front cover sheet. A range of assessment methods is used to evaluate student competency, including:

Written Questions
Direct Observation
Portfolio Development

Trainers and Assessors evaluate students by reviewing submitted written work and observing their performance in practical tasks.

The Trainer will clearly explain all assessment requirements, including how students will be assessed and what is expected for successful completion.

Assessment Methods

The following assessment methods are used across various units.

Please refer to the Delivery Sequence and Methods section of the Training & Assessment Strategy for unit-specific details:

🔹 Written Assessment

This includes written tests and questionnaires. Assessors will consider individual student needs and may provide reasonable adjustments where required to support fair assessment.

🔹 Direct Observation

Students are assessed in a simulated salon environment through practical tasks. These activities replicate real workplace conditions and may involve providing services to paying clients. Practical skills are observed for each unit of competency.

🔹 Portfolio

Students are required to compile a portfolio that may include research from online sources, hair magazines, brochures, retail and salon products, as well as completed pre-service analysis forms and other relevant documentation.

Course Overview

CHC30125 Certificate III in Early Childhood Education and Care reflects the role of educators working in regulated children’s education and care services in Australia. The qualification develops skills and knowledge to support children’s wellbeing, learning and development within an approved learning framework.

Early childhood educators may work in settings such as long day care services, family day care, pre-schools and kindergartens.

Why Study This Qualification?

✔︎ Develop practical skills relevant to early childhood education and care.

✔︎ Build knowledge of children’s health, safety, wellbeing, learning and development.

✔︎ Learn how to support inclusive and respectful relationships with children.

✔︎ Develop workplace skills through structured practical experience.

✔︎ Prepare for employment opportunities across the early childhood education and care sector.

✔︎ Create a pathway for further study in early childhood education and care.

Career Outcomes

Successful completion of CHC30125 can support employment in early childhood education and care settings, subject to applicable regulatory and employer requirements.

  • Early Childhood Educator
  • Child Care Worker
  • Family Day Care Educator
  • Early childhood education and care support roles
  • Other entry-level roles within regulated children’s education and care services, where the qualification meets the applicable requirements

This qualification is delivered through a blended model combining real-time virtual classroom delivery and face-to-face component.

Learners undertaking any online or digitally supported components should have access to a suitable computer or device, reliable internet connection, email and commonly used document/PDF software. Specific technology requirements should be confirmed by Fran Capelli Academy for the final delivery model.

Work placement is a mandatory component of CHC30125. Learners must complete a minimum of 160 hours of work in a regulated children’s education and care service in Australia, as required by the qualification and relevant unit assessment requirements.

Students are assessed in a simulated salon environment through practical tasks. These activities replicate real workplace conditions and may involve providing services to paying clients. Practical skills are observed for each unit of competency.

Students are required to compile a portfolio that may include research from online sources, hair magazines, brochures, retail and salon products, as well as completed pre-service analysis forms and other relevant documentation.

Course Overview

CHC30125 Certificate III in Early Childhood Education and Care reflects the role of educators working in regulated children’s education and care services in Australia. The qualification develops skills and knowledge to support children’s wellbeing, learning and development within an approved learning framework.

Early childhood educators may work in settings such as long day care services, family day care, pre-schools and kindergartens.

Why Study This Qualification?

✔︎ Develop practical skills relevant to early childhood education and care.

✔︎ Build knowledge of children’s health, safety, wellbeing, learning and development.

✔︎ Learn how to support inclusive and respectful relationships with children.

✔︎ Develop workplace skills through structured practical experience.

✔︎ Prepare for employment opportunities across the early childhood education and care sector.

✔︎ Create a pathway for further study in early childhood education and care.

Course Overview

CHC30125 Certificate III in Early Childhood Education and Care reflects the role of educators working in regulated children’s education and care services in Australia. The qualification develops skills and knowledge to support children’s wellbeing, learning and development within an approved learning framework.

Early childhood educators may work in settings such as long day care services, family day care, pre-schools and kindergartens.

Why Study This Qualification?

✔︎ Develop practical skills relevant to early childhood education and care.

✔︎ Build knowledge of children’s health, safety, wellbeing, learning and development.

✔︎ Learn how to support inclusive and respectful relationships with children.

✔︎ Develop workplace skills through structured practical experience.

✔︎ Prepare for employment opportunities across the early childhood education and care sector.

✔︎ Create a pathway for further study in early childhood education and care.

Career Outcomes

Successful completion of CHC30125 can support employment in early childhood education and care settings, subject to applicable regulatory and employer requirements.

  • Early Childhood Educator

  • Early childhood education and care support roles
  • Other entry-level roles within regulated children’s education and care services, where the qualification meets the applicable requirements

Delivery Method

This qualification is delivered through a blended model combining real-time virtual classroom delivery and face-to-face component.

Learners undertaking any online or digitally supported components should have access to a suitable computer or device, reliable internet connection, email and commonly used document/PDF software. Specific technology requirements should be confirmed by Fran Capelli Academy for the final delivery model.

Work Placement Requirements

Work placement is a mandatory component of CHC30125. Learners must complete a minimum of 160 hours of work in a regulated children’s education and care service in Australia, as required by the qualification and relevant unit assessment requirements.

  • Learners must complete the required National Child Safety Training before undertaking placement hours. (where applicable)

  • Students are responsible to secure an appropriate placement in a regulated early childhood education and care service. Fran Capelli Academy will provide guidance and reasonable assistance to help eligible students identify a suitable regulated early childhood education and care service.

Course Overview

This qualification is designed for students who want to become professional barbers without being employed under an apprenticeship contract. It provides the skills and knowledge required to perform a wide range of barbering services, including men’s haircutting, clipper techniques, beard and moustache design, shaving services, and men’s grooming. 

What will you learn?
  • Traditional and modern men's haircutting.
  • Clipper-over-comb and freehand clipper techniques.
  • Beard and moustache design and maintenance.
  • Head and face shaving.
  • Men's grooming services.
  • Client consultation and customer service.
  • Salon operations and workplace health and safety.
  • Basic hair coloring and highlighting services
Career Outcomes

• Qualified Barber 
• Men's Grooming Specialist 
• Barbershop Professional 
• Salon Barber Specialist

On Partial Completion of Course

Please note that awards will only be issued to students who have fulfilled all their financial obligations to Fran Capelli Academy.

For further information or to visit the Academy, please feel free to contact us on (03) 9818 0089.

Assessment Arrangements

Assessment Overview

This is a competency-based program, where assessment is conducted continuously throughout the course. Students are assessed until they either demonstrate competency in the required tasks or any identified learning gaps are addressed through further training.

Students are required to complete the written components of their assessments in their own time and submit them to their trainer by the specified due dates.

Assessment Requirements

Assessment requirements for each unit are clearly outlined on the front cover sheet. A range of assessment methods is used to evaluate student competency, including:

Written Questions
Direct Observation
Portfolio Development

Trainers and Assessors evaluate students by reviewing submitted written work and observing their performance in practical tasks.

The Trainer will clearly explain all assessment requirements, including how students will be assessed and what is expected for successful completion.

Assessment Methods

The following assessment methods are used across various units.

Please refer to the Delivery Sequence and Methods section of the Training & Assessment Strategy for unit-specific details:

🔹 Written Assessment

This includes written tests and questionnaires. Assessors will consider individual student needs and may provide reasonable adjustments where required to support fair assessment.

🔹 Direct Observation

Students are assessed in a simulated salon environment through practical tasks. These activities replicate real workplace conditions and may involve providing services to paying clients. Practical skills are observed for each unit of competency.

🔹 Portfolio

Students are required to compile a portfolio that may include research from online sources, hair magazines, brochures, retail and salon products, as well as completed pre-service analysis forms and other relevant documentation.

Frequently Asked Questions

Do I need to complete a trade apprenticeship to become a builder in South Australia?

Not necessarily. You can still qualify with the CPC40120 Certificate IV alone. However, you’ll need more proven experience usually around 5 years instead of 3 if you also have a trade apprenticeship and extra units.

How long does it take to become a licensed builder in SA?

It usually takes between 3 to 6 years of relevant on-site experience. The exact time depends on your qualifications, whether you complete CPC40120, and how long your CBS licence application takes to be approved.

What’s the quickest way to get a builder licence in SA?

The fastest pathway is combining a trade apprenticeship with CPC40120 (or a higher qualification) plus a few additional units. This can reduce the experience requirement to around 3 years.

Can I become a registered builder without any formal qualifications?

Yes, it’s possible but it takes longer. You’ll need about 6 years of relevant experience along with proof of at least 5 completed projects.

Does the “5 completed projects” requirement apply to all types of building work?

No. This requirement mainly applies to residential work (Class 1 & 10). Other areas like single-trade or civil construction may have different and sometimes more flexible requirements.

Is the process different for commercial or civil builders?

Yes. Commercial and civil construction licences usually have different requirements, often needing more advanced qualifications or longer experience due to the complexity of the work.

First, Understand the Two Licencing Requirements

Depending on how you intend to work in South Australia's building and construction industry, you may need a Building Work Supervisor Registration, a Building Work Contractor Licence, or both.

Verified Pathway

Building Work Supervisor Registration

A Building Work Supervisor is responsible for performing or supervising the technical building work and ensuring the work is completed to the required standards.

Your eligibility depends on the type and scope of building work you intend to undertake, as well as your qualifications, technical knowledge and relevant industry experience.

• Demonstrate relevant qualifications and practical industry experience.
• Complete the CBS assessment process applicable to your registration pathway.
• Include a technical interview assessed against the relevant performance criteria.
• Relates to the technical performance and supervision of building work.

Building Work Contractor Licence

A Building Work Contractor Licence allows you to carry on a building business and contract directly with clients for building work covered by your licence.

• May require completion of relevant CBS business knowledge units.
• Requires applicants to satisfy CBS's fit and proper person requirements.
• Financial and insurance requirements may apply depending on the circumstances.
• A contractor must have an appropriately registered Building Work Supervisor in place for the building work being undertaken.
• Holding a contractor licence does not, by itself, establish that you are qualified to personally supervise all technical building work.

Frequently Asked Questions

What’s the difference between supervisor registration and a contractor licence?

Supervisor registration covers the technical side of building work, including carrying out or supervising work. A contractor licence allows you to operate the business and enter into contracts with clients. Sole traders will generally need both.

Can I start doing building work while my application is being processed?

You generally need the appropriate licence and registration before you can contract for or supervise building work under that condition. Check with CBS about current processing times so you know what to expect.

Do I need the complete Certificate IV, or are the six business units enough?

For the contractor licence business requirement, you generally only need the units currently accepted by CBS, which may include six specific units. CPC40120 includes these units as part of the full 19-unit qualification and may be a better option if you want the complete qualification.

Is online study accepted for the business criteria units?

No. Completing the qualification does not automatically give you a licence or registration. CBS assesses your qualifications, experience and other requirements as part of the application process.

Do I need another Police Certificate if I recently provided one to CBS?

Not always. If you have provided a National Police Certificate to CBS within the previous 12 months, or supplied one for another licence under the same Act, you may not need a new one. Check with CBS to confirm your situation.

FRAN CAPELLI ACADEMY

Student Services - South Australia

Skills SA Subsidised Students

End-to-end support from your first conversation with us, throughout your training, and as you move towards completion and your next opportunity.

Student Services - South Australia

Practical, respectful and individualised support to help you participate in training, make progress and work toward successful completion.

Fran Capelli Academy is committed to providing an inclusive and supportive learning environment. We understand that every student brings different experience, skills, responsibilities and support needs. Our team will work with you before enrolment and throughout your training to identify reasonable and appropriate support that may help you succeed.

Fran Capelli Academy

Eligibility Criteria

Participant Eligibility Criteria apply to South Australian Government subsidised training. Eligibility, course availability and funding conditions must be confirmed before enrolment.

Check Eligibility Enroll Now

Support Available to You

Pre-enrolment guidance

Course information, entry requirements, suitability discussions and help understanding the enrolment process.

Language, literacy and numeracy

Assessment of your current skills and a support plan or referral where additional foundation skills assistance is needed.

Reasonable adjustment

Adjustments for disability, injury, health conditions or other individual needs, where these do not compromise the training product requirements.

Learning and trainer support

Clarification of learning activities, feedback, study planning, additional explanations and scheduled support.

Digital learning support

Help accessing the learning platform, online classes, digital resources and the technology used in your course.

Success and wellbeing support

Free and confidential non-clinical support for eligible subsidised students experiencing barriers that may affect training.

Upfront Assessment of Need (UAN)

Students seeking access to Skills SA subsidised training must complete the applicable Upfront Assessment of Need process before a training account is created. The UAN have the following assessment areas as mentioned below:

1. Pre-Training Review (PTR)

A discussion about your goals, previous education and work experience, course expectations, entry requirements, delivery arrangements, and whether the qualification is suitable for your individual needs.

2. ACER CSPA Assessment

A supervised Language, Literacy and Numeracy (LLN) assessment used to identify your reading, numeracy and, where applicable, writing skills. The results help determine whether additional learning support may be beneficial during your training.

3. Enrolment

Students who successfully complete the PTR and ACER CSPA assessment will be invited to complete the enrolment process before commencing their training.

Important: The UAN is not designed to prevent students from accessing training. Its purpose is to ensure the qualification is appropriate for you and to identify any support that may assist you to successfully complete your studies. In some cases, participation in agreed support services may be a condition of accessing Skills SA subsidised training.

Language, Literacy, Numeracy and Foundation Skills Support

Fran Capelli Academy is committed to supporting students to successfully complete their training.

Personal Learning Support

If additional language, literacy, numeracy (LLN) or digital skills support is identified, we may provide personalised learning support, reasonable adjustments where appropriate, and referrals to approved foundation skills or specialist support services.

Success and Wellbeing Services (SWS)

Success and Wellbeing Services (SWS) does not provide LLN tuition. Where foundation skills support is required, we will discuss the most appropriate support pathway and, with your consent, refer you to our approved LLN consultants.

LLN Consultants

Trisha Doecke – 0475 240 690
Bev Munchenberg – 0429 992 736
Email: cspa.interpretations@outlook.com

Success and Wellbeing Services (SWS)

Free, flexible and confidential support for eligible students in Skills SA subsidised training

Success and Wellbeing Services is funded by the South Australian Government and delivered by an approved SWS provider. The service provides non-clinical, individualised support to help students address barriers that may affect their ability to remain engaged in training and complete their course.

No cost

There is no charge to eligible students.

Confidential

Your privacy is respected and information is handled in accordance with applicable requirements.

Dedicated support

An experienced Success and Wellbeing Coach works with you to identify practical next steps.

Flexible contact

Support may be available in person, by phone, video call, email, text or outreach.

Available early

You can seek support before challenges become more difficult.

Post-course support

Support may continue for up to 12 weeks after you complete or leave your course.

SWS Providers Contact Details

FCA has Partnership Agreements with the following three Skills SA-approved SWS providers. You can contact any of them directly: 

Provider

Enhance Training

Phone

8462 0222

Email / Contact

sws@hesselgroup.com.au hesselgroup.com.au/enhance-training

What an SWS Coach may help with
  • Balancing training with work, family or caring responsibilities
  • Housing, transport or financial pressures
  • Grief, relationship difficulties or other personal circumstances
  • Stress, low motivation, anxiety, low mood or feeling overwhelmed
  • Connecting with health, community, cultural or specialist services
  • Developing practical routines to remain engaged in training
  • Advocacy or communication with Fran Capelli Academy, where you consent 
  • Transition planning for further study or employment.
Who can access SWS?

SWS is intended for eligible students participating in South Australian Government subsidised VET who may benefit from additional support to commence, continue or complete their training. Eligibility and referral arrangements are confirmed under current Skills SA requirements.

How to access Success and Wellbeing Services
  1. Talk to your Fran Capelli Academy trainer or Student Services team and ask us to arrange a referral.
  2. Self-refer through the Skills SA My Training website by locating the SWS provider linked to Fran Capelli Academy.
  3. Contact Fran Capelli Academy if you are unsure which option applies to you.

Fran Capelli Academy will discuss a proposed referral with you. Where consent is required, we will obtain it before sharing personal information with the SWS provider, except where disclosure is otherwise authorised or required by law.

SWS is not an emergency, crisis, medical or clinical mental health service. A coach can, however, help connect you with an appropriate service. In an immediate emergency, call 000.

Support for Apprentices and Trainees

Apprentices and trainees can experience additional pressures because training is combined with employment and workplace responsibilities. Fran Capelli Academy may work with you, your employer and relevant apprenticeship network or government stakeholders to support progress, subject to privacy and consent requirements.
> Clarifying the training plan, delivery schedule and workplace evidence requirements
> Coordinating trainer contact and workplace visits
> Identifying barriers affecting participation or progression
> Discussing suitable support or reasonable adjustment
> Helping address gaps in access to workplace tasks or supervision
> Referring eligible students to SWS or other support services

Privacy, Consent and Respectful Support

Information you provide about your support needs will be handled respectfully and in accordance with Fran Capelli Academy’s privacy obligations, contractual requirements and relevant policies. We only collect information that is reasonably necessary for enrolment, training, assessment, support, reporting or other authorised purposes.

Contact Fran Capelli Academy Student Services

Reach out as early as possible. You do not need to wait until a problem becomes serious before asking for assistance

Organisation: Fran Capelli Academy Pty Ltd

RTO number: 6055

South Australia office: 1–3 Metro Parade, Mawson Lakes SA 5095

Phone: 08 7137 1433

Email: enquiries@fca.edu.au

Online support and information:

Skills SA – My Training | Reach out to an SWS provider

Contact us

Frequently Asked Questions

Do I have to pay for SWS?

No. SWS is funded by the South Australian Government and is free for eligible students.

Will asking for support affect my enrolment?

Asking for support will not disadvantage you. Identifying needs early helps Fran Capelli Academy plan appropriate assistance. In some circumstances, engaging with an agreed support service may be a condition of access to subsidised training.

Is SWS counselling or medical treatment?

No. SWS is a non-clinical support and case management service. A coach may connect you with an appropriate medical, mental health, crisis or community service.

Can SWS help with reading, writing or numeracy?

SWS does not deliver literacy and numeracy training. Fran Capelli Academy will discuss foundation skills support or an approved referral pathway with you.

Can I ask for reasonable adjustment?

Yes. Contact Student Services or your trainer as early as possible. Adjustments are considered individually and must preserve the integrity of the training and assessment requirements.

Can I contact SWS directly?

Eligible students may be able to self-refer through the Skills SA My Training website, or Fran Capelli Academy can help arrange a referral.

How long is SWS available?

Current Skills SA information states that support is available from enrolment, throughout training and for up to 12 weeks after course completion or exit.

Competency & Support

To be eligible for this course, prospective students must be at least 18 years of age.

All applicants are required to successfully complete a Language, Literacy, Numeracy (LLN) assessment, along with a pre-training review/interview. This process, also referred to as an Upfront Assessment of Need (UAN), is conducted to ensure the course is suitable and aligned with the individual’s skills, experience, and learning needs.

The pre-training review helps identify the applicant’s existing knowledge, capabilities, and any support requirements to ensure they are set up for success throughout the course.

 
Course Structure

To achieve this qualification, the candidate must demonstrate competency in:

  • 19 units of competency:

    • 11 core units

    • 8 elective units.

To achieve the occupational outcome of Builder electives must include:

  • All Group A elective units

  • Up to two elective units from either Group B or general electives.

  • One elective unit may be from any training package or accredited course as long as it ensures the integrity of the qualification’s Australian Qualification Framework (AQF) alignment and contributes to a valid, industry supported vocational outcome

To achieve the occupation outcome of Site Manager electives must include:

  • All Group B electives

  • Up to four elective units from either Group A or general electives.

  • One unit may be from any training package or accredited course as long as it ensures the integrity of the qualification’s Australian Qualification Framework (AQF) alignment and contributes to a valid, industry supported vocational outcome

Melbourne (Online)

Adelaide (Online)

Entry Requirements

There are no entry requirements for this qualification

Course Duration

The course duration  is typically 36 weeks (Excluding Holidays)

Training Arrangements

Class Delivery and Learning Expectations

Classes are conducted once per week, offering a well-balanced mix of practical and theoretical learning. Each session is designed to accommodate diverse learning styles while supporting the development of the skills and knowledge required for successful course completion.

Practical workplace scenarios will be regularly simulated to assess your skills in line with the requirements of each unit.

In addition to attending classes, students are expected to commit to independent study each week, including:

  • Up to 7 hours of self-directed learning, such as revision, research, and engagement with course materials.
  • Up to 7 hours dedicated to assignment preparation, including completing assessments, reviewing feedback, and gathering evidence of competency.

Homework tasks may involve research activities, textbook readings, and ongoing work on assessments. All necessary learning resources will be provided at the start of each unit.

On Completion of Course

Students completing all assessment requirements will be awarded CPC40120 Certificate IV in Building and Construction.

​

On Partial Completion of Course

Students completing assessment requirements for part of CPC40120 Certificate IV in Building and Construction, will be awarded a statement of attainment indicating which modules or units of competency they have completed.  Awards will not be made to students who have not met all their financial commitments to Fran capelli Academy.

Course Overview

This qualification reflects the role of hairdressers who use a range of well-developed sales, consultation and technical skills and knowledge to provide a broad range of hairdressing services to clients. They use discretion and judgement to provide client services and take responsibility for the outcomes of their own work.
This qualification provides a pathway to work as a hairdresser in any industry environment, usually a salon.
No occupational licensing, certification or specific legislative requirements apply to this qualification at the time of publication.

What will you learn?

You will learn how to:

cut, colour, chemically reform and style your client's hair.

You will also learn about client communication and service which includes discussing the needs of your client and styling according to their requirements.

Career Outcomes
  • Hairdresser in professional salons
  • Salon Stylist
  • Hair Color Specialist
  • Can seek employment as qualified hairdressers in salons and related industry settings

Entry Requirments

If you would like any further information or come in and see the Academy please don’t hesitate to contact us on (03) 9818 0089.

Assessment Arrangements

Assessment Overview

This is a competency-based program, where assessment is conducted continuously throughout the course. Students are assessed until they either demonstrate competency in the required tasks or any identified learning gaps are addressed through further training.

Students are required to complete the written components of their assessments in their own time and submit them to their trainer by the specified due dates.

Assessment Requirements

Assessment requirements for each unit are clearly outlined on the front cover sheet. A range of assessment methods is used to evaluate student competency, including:

Written Questions
Direct Observation
Portfolio Development

Trainers and Assessors evaluate students by reviewing submitted written work and observing their performance in practical tasks.

The Trainer will clearly explain all assessment requirements, including how students will be assessed and what is expected for successful completion.

Assessment Methods

The following assessment methods are used across various units.

Please refer to the Delivery Sequence and Methods section of the Training & Assessment Strategy for unit-specific details:

🔹 Written Assessment

This includes written tests and questionnaires. Assessors will consider individual student needs and may provide reasonable adjustments where required to support fair assessment.

🔹 Direct Observation

Students are assessed in a simulated salon environment through practical tasks. These activities replicate real workplace conditions and may involve providing services to paying clients. Practical skills are observed for each unit of competency.

🔹 Portfolio

Students are required to compile a portfolio that may include research from online sources, hair magazines, brochures, retail and salon products, as well as completed pre-service analysis forms and other relevant documentation.

Frequently Asked Questions

What courses do you offer?

We offer nationally recognised vocational courses, including:

  • CHC30125 Certificate III in Early Childhood Education and Care
  • CPC50220 Diploma of Building and Construction (Building)
  • CPC40120 Certificate IV in Building and Construction
  • SHB30516 Certificate III in Barbering (Apprenticeship)
  • SHB30516 Certificate III in Barbering (Non-Apprenticeship)
  • SHB30416 Certificate III in Hairdressing (Apprenticeship)
  • SHB30416 Certificate III in Hairdressing (Non-Apprenticeship)
Who can apply for your courses?

Our courses are open to school leavers, job seekers, career changers, apprentices, and anyone looking to gain practical skills and nationally recognised qualifications.

Do I need previous experience before enrolling?

No. Many of our programs are designed for beginners. Some courses may have specific entry requirements, and our admissions team can help you determine the best course for your background and career goals.

What is the difference between apprenticeship and non-apprenticeship courses?

Apprenticeship courses combine workplace employment with formal training, allowing students to earn while they learn. Non-apprenticeship courses are ideal for individuals who want to study full-time or part-time without being employed as an apprentice.

Will I receive a nationally recognised qualification?

Yes. Students who successfully complete their course will receive the relevant nationally recognised qualification, subject to meeting all course requirements.

Are your courses practical?

Yes. Our training combines classroom learning with hands-on practical experience, helping students develop the skills and confidence required in real workplaces.

What career opportunities are available after completing these courses?

Graduates may pursue careers such as:

  • Site Supervisor
  • Construction Manager
  • Building Estimator
  • Barber
  • Hairdresser
  • Salon Professional
  • Small Business Owner

Career opportunities depend on the qualification completed and relevant industry requirements.

What is Nationally Recognised Training?

Nationally Recognised Training is vocational education and training delivered by a Registered Training Organisation (RTO) and recognised across Australia. Successfully completing a nationally recognised course means you receive a qualification or Statement of Attainment that is accepted by employers and other education providers nationwide.
